news.title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente
news.lede: Spain head coach hits out at ‘acts of aggression’. Fifa investigation into incident yet to result in sanctions. Spain’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has hit out at the “intolerable, unacceptable” behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s World Cup final. At the forefront were Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes, who attacked Rodri and Eric García respectively at New York New Jersey Stadium as Spain’s players celebrated winning the World Cup for a second time in the country’s history.

news.title: World Cup match-fixing probe sparked after suspicious Spain match
news.lede: One of Spain’s matches on their way to winning the 2026 FIFA World Cup became the subject of a match-fixing probe. Spain won the tournament thanks to a 1-0 victory over Argentina in the final, having triumphed in all but one of their seven matches on their way to the climax at MetLife Stadium. The exception was a goalless draw with Cape Verde in their opening match of the World Cup, and the game was flagged as suspicious by the Council of Europe's betting monitoring unit, the Group of Copenhagen. Investigators were thought to be left surprised that Cape Verde managed to hold Spain to a goalless draw, and the match was played on ‘yellow notice’, meaning further investigation was required.

news.title: Spain coach De la Fuente says Argentina’s conduct after World Cup final was ‘unacceptable’
news.lede: GENEVA (AP) — As FIFA investigates Argentina’s conduct after the World Cup final, Spain coach Luis de la Fuente has described the incidents as “intolerable and unacceptable.” FIFA asked one of its disciplinary prosecutors Monday to report back on testy on-field confrontations after Spain’s 1-0 win in extra time Sunday to dethrone the defending champion. Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes physically tangled with Spain players Eric Garcia and Gavi, and Spain captain Rodri was hit in the stomach as he ran past Argentina defender Nahuel Molina.

news.title: Germany Turns to Jurgen Klopp to Rebuild National Team Before 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Germany appointed Jurgen Klopp as head coach on Thursday, July 24, 2026, handing the former Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool manager his first job in international football after more than two decades at club level. The German Football Association made the appointment following Germany’s disappointing campaign at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, in which the team’s elimination ended Julian Nagelsmann’s tenure. Klopp, 59, now takes charge with preparations already focused on UEFA Euro 2028 and qualification for the 2030 FIFA World Cup. The announcement ends months of speculation over who would guide one of international football’s most successful national teams into its next competitive cycle.

news.title: Feeling lost without the World Cup? Six ways to survive the weekend
news.lede: What to watch on TV plus other ways to occupy your time now that the party is over. The 2026 World Cup is over, and the millions of people who enjoyed it now find themselves presented with a yawning chasm this weekend. In the UK alone, ITV and the BBC broadcast approximately 275 hours of live coverage over the duration of the tournament, and something that colossal will be hard to replace. Just because the football is over, we are still brimming with things similarly designed to take our minds off the screaming hellpit that is the world around us.

news.lede: Leandro Paredes has admitted he is uncertain about his international future following Argentina's painful FIFA World Cup final defeat to Spain, with the midfielder reflecting on a tournament-ending loss overshadowed by his involvement in the chaotic post-match altercation. Football News: Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes reflects on his uncertain future with the national team following a chaotic World Cup final loss to Spain, where he was involved in a post-match brawl. Paredes expresses pride in the team's journey but faces a tough decision about continuing his international career after epic disappointment.

news.title: Inside Nike’s ‘Rip the Script’ World Cup campaign
news.lede: The World Cup wrapped last Sunday, with Spain beating Argentina in a nailbiter of a final that scored 62.8 million viewers in the US. For some soccer fans, the final whistle marked the end of a whirlwind few weeks. For Nike, the tournament was just the beginning. “The actual, most exciting challenge starts today,” Camilo Andrade, global VP and GM football/soccer at Nike, told Marketing Brew the week after the tournament.
